patient_information: A 24-year-old man of Turkish origin, residing in Germany. He had a known history of cystic echinococcosis (CE), diagnosed three years prior with two calcified liver cysts confirmed by imaging and positive serology for Echinococcus granulosus.
chief_complaint: Right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with acute right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting. Three years earlier, he was diagnosed with cystic echinococcosis after presenting with similar pain. At that time, an ultrasound and CT scan revealed two calcified cystic lesions in his liver. Serology was positive for Echinococcus granulosus. Since the cyst walls were calcified and he was asymptomatic, anthelmintic treatment was not offered and he refused surgical treatment. The cysts were monitored by ultrasound.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is a resident of Germany but visits his family in rural eastern Turkey (Anatolia), a hyperendemic region for cystic echinococcosis, every year for about 6 weeks.
vitals: Blood pressure was 110/70 mmHg, pulse was 64 bpm, and temperature was 36°C (96.8°F).
physical_exam: The patient was in fair general condition with scleral jaundice. There was right upper quadrant and epigastric tenderness on palpation, but no guarding.
labs_and_diagnostics: The full blood count was normal. An endoscopic retrograde cholangiography (ERC) revealed biliary obstruction caused by a cystobiliary fistula, and cyst content was found in the common bile duct. Imaging from three years prior had identified two liver cysts: one 7 x 6 cm in the right lobe (WHO classification CE3b) and another 5 x 4 cm in the left lobe (WHO classification CE1), both with calcified walls.
differential_diagnosis: The main differential diagnoses for cystic liver lesions in this patient included a congenital simple hepatic cyst and pseudocysts associated with alveolar echinococcosis (E. multilocularis). Other considerations included infectious causes like bacterial or amoebic abscesses or tuberculoma, as well as benign and malignant liver tumours or metastases.
management_and_clinical_course: An endoscopic retrograde cholangiography (ERC) was performed, during which cyst content was removed from the common bile duct, restoring bile flow. The patient's resulting cholangitis was treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. Once the inflammation settled, he was referred for surgery, and a partial cystectomy was performed on both cysts. He has been followed up for 9 years after surgery with no recurrence and is considered cured.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis was complicated cystic echinococcosis due to the larval form of the tapeworm Echinococcus granulosus. The patient's known CE, with risk from travel to rural Turkey, presented as a cystobiliary fistula causing biliary obstruction and cholangitis. The diagnosis was confirmed by endoscopic retrograde cholangiography (ERC) which visualized the fistula and cyst material in the bile duct. His complete recovery following targeted treatment including surgical cystectomy solidified the diagnosis.
